items.label: Reset Zone
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > top
items.does: Puts this one zone back to its defaults (finish, colour, patterns, sliders).
items.when: The zone is a mess and you want a clean start for it only.
items.mistakes: It resets the zone, not the whole car - Reset All Zones in the left column does that.

items.label: COLOR (section)
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > COLOR
items.does: Decides WHICH PIXELS of the paint this zone owns: by clicked colour, by PSD layer, or as catch-all (Remaining).
items.when: A buyer says "only the red parts" or "only the numbers".
items.mistakes: A zone with no colour, layer or box set does nothing ("No color or region set yet" warning).

items.label: RESTRICT TO LAYERS (checkboxes per PSD layer)
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > COLOR > RESTRICT TO LAYERS
items.does: Tick a layer (Car Paint, Sponsors, Numbers, Tape ...) and the zone only covers pixels that exist on that layer.
items.when: Put a finish on just the numbers / sponsors / tape, or only the body paint, with no colour bleed.
items.mistakes: Layers named Mask / Wire / Car_Mandatory are template layers - do not restrict to them. Unticking everything (All layers) removes the restriction.

items.label: PICK COLOR FROM CAR
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > COLOR
items.does: Arms an eyedropper: click a colour on the car and this zone grabs every pixel of that colour. Each further click ADDS another colour.
items.when: Select one colour area (the red stripe, the green body) without drawing anything.
items.mistakes: Anti-aliased edges need tolerance; if edges are left over raise tolerance. Colours that also appear on logos need a layer or box restriction.

items.label: Remaining
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > COLOR
items.does: Makes this zone the catch-all: it gets every pixel no zone above it claims.
items.when: The classic body zone - "everything else".
items.mistakes: Put it at the BOTTOM of the zone list; higher zones win overlaps.

items.label: HEX (colour box and colour wheel) + Apply
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > COLOR
items.does: Type or pick a colour to select by (with Apply), or use the wheel which applies live.
items.when: You know the exact colour of the area you want to select.
items.mistakes: This chooses which paint pixels to catch, it does not recolour them. To RECOLOUR use BASE > Base Color > Use solid color.

items.label: Colour tolerance (sliders next to the colour chips)
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > COLOR
items.does: How close a pixel must be to the picked colour to belong to the zone (about 30-50 normal; 6 = exact shade, 100 = loose).
items.when: The edges of the area look chewed (raise it) or neighbours get caught (lower it).
items.mistakes: Too high grabs neighbouring colours; too low leaves fringes around lettering.

items.label: Hard Edge
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > COLOR
items.does: Cuts the zone edge sharp instead of softly anti-aliased.
items.when: Crisp lettering and thin lines are getting fuzzy edges.
items.mistakes: Hard edges can look jagged on diagonal lines.

items.label: APPLY AREA (section)
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > APPLY AREA
items.does: Limits the zone to a drawn shape (box or lasso) or a refined colour area, on top of the colour/layer choice.
items.when: Only the hood, only the left side, only the bottom half.
items.mistakes: "Draw box" boxes are on the flat unwrapped sheet; one box may cover several car panels.

items.label: Draw box
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > APPLY AREA
items.does: Click, then drag a rectangle on the paint; the zone only affects what is inside it.
items.when: Quick way to restrict a zone to one panel.
items.mistakes: The box is on the flat sheet - the hood and the roof are different rectangles, not one.

items.label: Lasso (apply area)
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > APPLY AREA
items.does: Draw a free-hand outline; the zone only affects what is inside.
items.when: The area to restrict is not a rectangle.
items.mistakes: Close the shape by returning near the start point.

items.label: Refine color
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > APPLY AREA
items.does: Keeps the colour selection but lets you paint a green brush to limit it to places you choose.
items.when: The colour also shows up where you do not want it.
items.mistakes: Needs a colour already set on the zone.

items.label: Activate (apply area)
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > APPLY AREA
items.does: Turns the stored apply area on again after you cleared or paused it.
items.when: You drew an area earlier and it is no longer limiting the zone.

items.label: Clear (apply area)
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > APPLY AREA
items.does: Removes the drawn box / lasso so the zone is back to colour/layer only.
items.when: The zone is only showing in a box you drew by mistake.

items.label: Fit pattern/base swatch into box
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > APPLY AREA
items.does: Instead of tiling across the sheet, fit one copy of the pattern / base texture into the drawn box.
items.when: One big logo-like pattern placed in one area.
items.mistakes: Only base + pattern are fitted, not spec overlays.

items.label: BASE (section)
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE
items.does: Everything about the surface look: finish, colour source, hue / saturation / brightness, strengths, scale, rotation, spec sliders.
items.when: A buyer says "make it chrome / matte / candy / shinier".
items.mistakes: Without picking a finish the zone shows source paint unchanged.

items.label: Base Material (finish picker button)
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE
items.does: Opens the finish picker popup: bases (gloss, matte, satin, chrome, candy, pearl, metallic ...) and special looks. Shows the current finish name.
items.when: Choose or change the finish of this zone.
items.mistakes: Foundation (f_*) finishes change only the spec when colour = Use source paint; bases like chrome / candy repaint the zone.

items.label: Lock (Base Color lock)
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE > Base Color
items.does: When on, switching finish keeps your zone colour instead of auto-adopting the finish's default colour.
items.when: Auto colour change keeps overwriting the colour you chose.

items.label: BASE COLOR dropdown
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE > Base Color
items.does: Where the zone colour comes from: Use finish's own color / Use source paint (spec only) / Use solid color / From special / Custom gradient.
items.when: "Keep my colours, change only the shine" (source), "make it exactly this colour" (solid), "fade" (gradient).
items.mistakes: Solid colour on a finish that brings its own colours (carbon, camo, holographic ...) flattens it to one colour and loses the pattern: use Hue Shift instead. If a colour 'will not apply', check this dropdown first.

items.label: Solid colour swatch / hex (appears with Use solid color)
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE > Base Color
items.does: Paints the zone this exact colour with the finish's shine on top.
items.when: The buyer names an exact colour.
items.mistakes: Only used when BASE COLOR = Use solid color.

items.label: Custom gradient (stops + direction)
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE > Base Color (after choosing Custom gradient)
items.does: 2 to 10 colour stops fading across the zone in a chosen direction.
items.when: "Fade from red to black".
items.mistakes: Direction runs on the flat sheet, so each car side may fade differently - use one zone per side to control it.

items.label: Hue Shift
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE
items.does: Rotates every colour around the colour wheel (-180 to +180). Keeps the finish's structure.
items.when: Recolour a finish that brings its own colours, or tweak a colour a bit.
items.mistakes: Shift = target hue minus current hue; +150 on green gives purple, not pink.

items.label: Saturation
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE
items.does: How vivid or grey the colour is (-100 to +100).
items.when: Colours look washed out or too loud.

items.label: Brightness
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE
items.does: Lighter or darker (-100 to +200).
items.when: Make a colour darker or lighter without changing the finish.

items.label: Base Strength
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE
items.does: Fades the whole base look over the source paint: 0 = original paint, 100 = full finish.
items.when: A subtle hint of the finish instead of full coverage.
items.mistakes: This also reduces colour changes; for shine only use Spec Strength.

items.label: Spec Strength
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE
items.does: Overall strength of the spec map (shine / metal / coat) of this zone.
items.when: Make the finish less (or more) reflective without moving the colour.

items.label: Base Scale
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE
items.does: Size of the finish's texture inside this zone (0.05x to 5.0x; 1.00x is normal). Smaller = finer, more repeats.
items.when: Texture too coarse or too fine (carbon, flake, camo look huge on the whole car).
items.mistakes: Scales the texture, NOT the colours or the whole car; spec follows it unless Independent Spec is ticked.

items.label: Base Rotation
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE
items.does: Rotates the finish's texture in 5 degree steps.
items.when: Weave or brushed grain runs the wrong way.

items.label: Color Depth
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE
items.does: For candy / tinted finishes: 0 = no tint, 15 = glaze, 65 = rich, 100 = deepest.
items.when: Candy looks pale or too dark.
items.mistakes: Only shows on candy-like finishes.

items.label: Color Flip
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE
items.does: Adds a second hue that appears at an angle (0 = off, 90 = neighbour, 180 = opposite).
items.when: Colour-shifting paint.
items.mistakes: Only on finishes that support it.

items.label: Underglow
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE
items.does: How much of the ground coat burns through the brights.
items.when: More glow in highlights on candy / flip paints.

items.label: Independent Spec (checkbox by Spec Scale)
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE
items.does: Lets Spec Scale differ from Base Scale; otherwise spec follows the base size.
items.when: Want the shine texture finer or coarser than the colour texture.

items.label: Spec Scale
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE
items.does: Size of the shine / metal texture (0.05x-5.0x) when independent.
items.when: Fine shine detail under a coarse colour pattern.
items.mistakes: Ignored until Independent Spec is ticked.

items.label: Spec Rotation
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE
items.does: Rotates the spec channels in 5 degree steps.
items.when: Brushed grain in the shine runs the wrong way.

items.label: Spec Blend
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE
items.does: How a pattern changes this base's optics: Normal, Ghost Carve, Chrome Inlay, Frost Etch, Angle Flip, Ember Gate, Depth Press, and legacy Multiply / Screen / Overlay modes.
items.when: Pattern should alter shine / metal rather than just brightness.

items.label: Spec Sliders (R Metal, G Rough, B Coat)
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE > Spec Sliders
items.does: Three sliders (-127 to +127) that push the whole zone's spec map: R = metal, G = roughness (low = mirror), B = clearcoat.
items.when: Make the zone shinier / more metallic / matte without changing the finish: "make the spec shinier only".
items.mistakes: B Coat is inverted in iRacing terms - the number moves clearcoat strength, see the tooltip. Spec only changes in the spec map and in iRacing; the flat colour preview may look unchanged.

items.label: Auto-Pop
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE > Spec Sliders
items.does: One click nudges the three spec sliders toward glossier (more metal flash, less rough, deeper clearcoat) so the zone pops on track.
items.when: Fast "make it shinier" without thinking about channels.
items.mistakes: It nudges from where the sliders are; press repeatedly for more, Reset arrows to go back.

items.label: Spec preset... dropdown
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE > Spec Sliders
items.does: Applies a named spec feel (Wet Candy, Track Flash, Chrome Mirror, Deep Gloss, Soft Pearl, Satin Matte) to the R/G/B sliders.
items.when: You want a known shine character.

items.label: Save spec preset (disk icon)
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE > Spec Sliders
items.does: Saves this zone's R/G/B spec shifts under a name you can reuse.
items.when: You found a shine you like.

items.label: R Metal
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE > Spec Sliders
items.does: Pushes the METAL channel (-127 to +127). More metal = the body colour flashes harder.
items.when: Metal looks too weak or too much.

items.label: G Rough
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE > Spec Sliders
items.does: Pushes ROUGHNESS (-127 to +127). Lower = sharper mirror flashes, higher = soft satin glow.
items.when: Too shiny or too dull.

items.label: B Coat
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE > Spec Sliders
items.does: Pushes CLEARCOAT (-127 to +127). 16 is max gloss: minus = glossier (stops at 16), plus = duller.
items.when: Wants a glassier or flatter clearcoat.

items.label: SPEC OVERLAYS + ADD SPEC OVERLAY
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE > SPEC OVERLAYS
items.does: Stack spec-only textures on top of the base: they change shine / metal / roughness patterns, never the colour.
items.when: Brushed metal, hammered, scratched or carbon-weave SHINE under flat colour.
items.mistakes: Colour preview will not show them; look at the spec channel views.

items.label: + ADD SPEC OVERLAY
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE > SPEC OVERLAYS
items.does: Opens the spec-overlay picker to add one more spec texture layer.
items.when: Add a shine texture.
items.mistakes: Up to 5 layers on the primary base.

items.label: PATTERN (section)
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > PATTERN
items.does: Adds a visible pattern (carbon, camo, flames, stripes ...) on this zone, with Paint mode, Opacity, Strength, Hue, Saturation, Spec amount, Scale, Rotate and Position.
items.when: A buyer wants a pattern on the paint.

items.label: Pattern 1 picker (name + dropdown arrow)
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > PATTERN
items.does: Choose the pattern from the catalogue; "None" (x) removes it.
items.when: Add or remove a pattern.

items.label: + Add Layer (pattern)
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > PATTERN
items.does: Adds a second / third pattern layer to the zone.
items.when: Combine patterns.

items.label: Paint mode (Overlay / Blend)
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > PATTERN
items.does: Overlay = the pattern paints its own colours over the paint; Blend = it keeps the underlying paint colour.
items.when: The pattern covers the colour you chose (use Blend), or will not take your colour.
items.mistakes: In Overlay the pattern's own colours win, so the base colour is hidden - use Blend or Hue to recolour.

items.label: Opacity (pattern)
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > PATTERN
items.does: How visible the pattern is, 0-100%.
items.when: Pattern too loud.

items.label: Strength (pattern)
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > PATTERN
items.does: Pattern paint strength in 5% steps; spec amount is separate.

items.label: Hue / Saturation (pattern)
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > PATTERN
items.does: Recolours only the pattern artwork (hue -180..180, saturation -100..100). Overlay mode uses this colour.
items.when: Pattern has the wrong colour but the base colour is right.

items.label: Spec amount (pattern)
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > PATTERN
items.does: Starts at 0% so your base shine stays; raise to reveal the pattern's own metal / rough / coat.
items.when: Pattern should also change the shine.
items.mistakes: Spec starts at 0 on purpose.

items.label: Scale (pattern)
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > PATTERN
items.does: Size of the pattern: smaller = more repeats, larger = zoomed in (0.1x to 4x).
items.when: "Crush the pattern finer", or make it bigger.
items.mistakes: On a whole-car canvas a normal-size pattern looks huge: go below 1.0x for fine detail.

items.label: Rotate (pattern)
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > PATTERN
items.does: Rotates the pattern 0-359 degrees (also a number box).
items.when: Stripes / weave at the wrong angle.

items.label: Pattern placement: Full Canvas / Fit to Zone / Edit on Template
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > PATTERN
items.does: Choose how the pattern is placed: tiled over the sheet, fitted to the zone, or dragged by hand on the template.
items.when: Place a pattern on one spot.

items.label: Advanced Pattern Control Panel (Position X / Y, Flip H / V, Strength Map)
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > PATTERN > Advanced Pattern Control Panel
items.does: Slide the pattern left/right and up/down, flip it, or paint where it is strong versus weak.
items.when: Fine placement.

items.label: OVERLAYS (2nd to 5th base)
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > OVERLAYS
items.does: Stack extra base finishes over the first with blend modes.
items.when: Chrome flake over candy, matte clear on gloss, etc.

items.label: 2nd Base (picker) + Add 3rd overlay
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > OVERLAYS
items.does: Pick a second finish blended on top of the primary base; "+ Add 3rd overlay" shows the next slot.
items.when: Two-layer looks.

items.label: Zone order (drag handle and priority)
items.where: Pro > left column > zone cards (drag the handle)
items.does: Top zone wins where two zones select the same pixels.
items.when: "Why is my zone not showing?" - another zone above it already claims those pixels.
items.mistakes: Remaining belongs at the bottom.

items.label: Zone eye / duplicate / link / x icons on each zone card
items.where: Pro > left column > zone card
items.does: Eye hides a zone for testing, the copy icon duplicates, the x deletes it.
items.when: Temporarily see the car without a zone; copy a zone to reuse its look.
items.mistakes: x removes the zone (undoable with Ctrl+Z).

items.label: Color Scale / Color Rotation
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > BASE (only with From special or Custom gradient)
items.does: Zooms and rotates the colour art (gradient or borrowed special colours) without touching the material texture.
items.when: The gradient or borrowed colours are too big, small or at the wrong angle.
items.mistakes: Solid colours have nothing to scale; these only appear for From special / Custom gradient.

items.label: Intensity (zone strength, legacy preset buttons)
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > zone header (if shown on your build)
items.does: Overall strength of the zone's effect: lower = closer to the original paint and a calmer spec.
items.when: Finish is too loud overall.
items.mistakes: Not seen in the live panel of build 10.0.3 (listed in app_controls.json); prefer Base Strength / Spec Strength.

items.label: Wear / weathering
items.where: Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; E shows / hides the panel) > wear slider (if shown on your build)
items.does: Scuffs and ages the finish (chips, dulling).
items.when: A worn / used look.
items.mistakes: Not seen in the live panel of build 10.0.3; check for a Wear control or ask Chat for a weathered finish.

items.label: Layer eye icon
items.where: Pro > LAYERS tab > layer row
items.does: Shows / hides the layer. Alt+click isolates that layer.
items.when: Turn template layers (Mask, Wire, Car_Mandatory) OFF before export; hide a sponsor to see the paint under it.
items.mistakes: Leaving Mask / Wire / Car_Mandatory on paints them into the car.

items.label: Layer opacity
items.where: Pro > LAYERS tab > layer row
items.does: Fades the layer 0-100% (drag, or type an exact number).
items.when: A sponsor or decal is too strong.

items.label: Layer blend mode
items.where: Pro > LAYERS tab > layer row
items.does: How the layer mixes with those below (Normal, Multiply, Screen, Overlay ...).
items.when: Wants a shadow / glow effect.

items.label: Layer lock
items.where: Pro > LAYERS tab > layer row
items.does: Locks the layer so it cannot be painted or changed.
items.when: Protect finished art.
items.mistakes: The Shokker AI cannot edit locked layers - unlock first.

items.label: Create a zone restricted to this layer
items.where: Pro > LAYERS tab > layer row (zone icon)
items.does: One click makes a zone that only covers this layer's pixels; then give it a finish.
items.when: "Make the numbers chrome": the quickest exact way.

items.label: Lock the active zone to this layer (Ctrl+L)
items.where: Pro > LAYERS tab > layer row
items.does: Restricts the currently selected zone to this layer.
items.when: You already have the zone and want it limited to one layer.

items.label: Rename / duplicate / delete / merge / flip / rotate / effects icons
items.where: Pro > LAYERS tab > layer row
items.does: Standard layer housekeeping: rename, duplicate (Shift = offset copy), delete, merge into the layer below, flip, rotate 90 degrees, Layer Effects (drop shadow, glow, stroke, colour overlay, bevel).
items.when: Fix or reuse art.
items.mistakes: Delete removes the layer art from the document; use the eye to just hide it.

items.label: Filter layers box
items.where: Pro > LAYERS tab > top right
items.does: Type part of a layer name or group to narrow a long list; Escape clears.
items.when: A PSD with dozens of layers.
items.mistakes: There is no sort-by-colour: the list is in PSD order. To work BY COLOUR use a zone with PICK COLOR FROM CAR.

items.label: Layer name (click) / Ctrl+click / double-click
items.where: Pro > LAYERS tab > layer row
items.does: Click selects the layer; Ctrl+click moves it on the canvas; double-click opens Layer Effects.
items.when: Edit just that layer.

items.label: Collapse arrow (left column)
items.where: Pro > left column edge
items.does: Collapses or expands the ZONES column.
items.when: More room for the canvas.

items.label: Collapse arrow (right column)
items.where: Pro > right column edge
items.does: Collapses or expands the FINISHES / LAYERS column.
items.when: More room for the canvas.

items.label: Zone editor tab (E)
items.where: Pro > left of the canvas
items.does: Shows or hides the floating ZONE POPOUT PANEL (press E).
items.when: The zone controls vanished or are in the way.

items.label: AI button (bottom right)
items.where: Pro > bottom right corner
items.does: Opens the Shokker AI panel (the copilot).
items.when: Wants to talk to the app.

items.label: Shokker AI panel
items.where: Pro / Chat > bottom right
items.does: Chat window: type what you want, the copilot changes zones and layers. Works with no key for common requests (colours, matte / gloss / chrome, stripes, spec looks).
items.when: "Make the hood matte black", "retro red white and blue".
items.mistakes: It cannot import files, export, or hand-paint; it can only tell the buyer where to click.

items.label: Tell me what you want... box
items.where: Shokker AI panel
items.does: Type your request; Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line.

items.label: Attach a picture
items.where: Shokker AI panel
items.does: Attach a livery you like, a logo or a flag; the AI can copy its design or colours (needs an AI key).
items.when: Copy the style of a picture.
items.mistakes: Cheap models cannot read UV sheets; results may need correcting.

items.label: Undo (under each answer)
items.where: Shokker AI panel
items.does: Puts everything back the way it was before that answer (all zones and layer changes of that answer).
items.when: The change was wrong.

items.label: Another take / Refine / Ask the AI
items.where: Shokker AI panel
items.does: Another try with a different idea; Refine looks at the preview and fixes what is off; Ask the AI undoes and lets the AI have a go.
items.when: Not happy with the first answer.

items.label: Gear (key, model, daily cap, Claude / ChatGPT connection)
items.where: Shokker AI panel > top
items.does: Settings: your OpenRouter key and model (one model only), a daily spending cap, and "Let an AI assistant (Claude or ChatGPT/Codex) control Shokker Paint Booth" with Install in Claude Desktop / Connect ChatGPT.
items.when: Wants a smarter copilot, or to use their own Claude / ChatGPT plan.
items.mistakes: The gear MODEL only applies to the in-app copilot; Claude Desktop uses its own model. Use Take over in SPB before asking the in-app copilot while an external assistant has control.

items.label: Use Claude Desktop through MCP
items.where: Shokker AI panel > gear
items.does: Install Shokker into Claude Desktop, then ask Claude "Using Shokker Paint Booth, give me a Gulf-style livery". Changes appear in the AI panel with Undo.
items.when: Wants Claude to design the livery with the buyer's own plan.
items.mistakes: Restart Claude Desktop after installing; Shokker must be open.

items.label: Connect ChatGPT / Codex
items.where: Shokker AI panel > gear > bridge settings
items.does: Add SPB to Codex settings, restart Codex and sign in with ChatGPT.
items.when: Wants ChatGPT / Codex to drive Shokker.
items.mistakes: Your subscription limits apply.

how_do_i.title: How do I load my paint file (a flat TGA, PNG or JPEG)?
steps: Top row, find SOURCE PAINT. Click the "TGA/PNG/JPEG" button beside it (or on the empty canvas click "Load TGA" / "Load Paint Image").
Pick your paint file in the window that opens, then confirm.
Wait for the paint to appear in the SOURCE picture in the middle; the LIVE PREVIEW fills in next.
You can also paste the full file path into the Source Paint box and press Enter.

how_do_i.title: How do I load a layered PSD template (so I get layers)?
steps: Top row, SOURCE PAINT, click the "PSD/XCF/ORA" button (or "Import PSD" on the empty canvas, or the LAYERS tab > "Open Layered").
Choose your PSD (XCF and ORA also work) and confirm.
Wait while the layers load, then open the LAYERS tab on the right to see them.
Before rendering, switch the template layers (Mask, Wire, Car_Mandatory) OFF with their eye icons.

how_do_i.title: How do I start from a blank canvas with no paint file?
steps: On the empty centre canvas click "Blank Canvas".
You get a plain white canvas to build colours on with zones and finishes.
Set the iRacing customer ID and car folder at the top before you render.

how_do_i.title: How do I switch between PRO and CHAT?
steps: At the top find the pill with PRO and CHAT.
Click the one you want. Your paint and zones stay open.

how_do_i.title: How do I make a zone?
steps: In the left ZONES column click "+ Add Zone". The new zone goes to the top and opens in the ZONE POPOUT PANEL.
In COLOR choose which pixels it covers: "PICK COLOR FROM CAR" then click the car, or tick a layer under RESTRICT TO LAYERS.
In BASE click Base Material and choose a finish.
Watch the LIVE PREVIEW. A zone needs BOTH an area (colour, layer or box) and a finish.

how_do_i.title: How do I put a finish on just one part of the car (the hood, the roof, one side)?
steps: Click "+ Add Zone".
In the ZONE POPOUT PANEL find APPLY AREA and click "Draw box".
Drag a box on the paint around that panel (the sheet is flat: hood, roof and sides are separate rectangles).
Under BASE click Base Material and pick the finish.

how_do_i.title: How do I change only one colour of my livery (say all the red)?
steps: Click "+ Add Zone".
In COLOR click "PICK COLOR FROM CAR", then click a red spot on the car. Raise the tolerance if red edges are left.
In BASE pick a finish.
To make it a different colour set the BASE COLOR dropdown to "Use solid color" and choose the colour.

how_do_i.title: How do I select a colour so a zone only affects that colour?
steps: Select the zone, open COLOR.
Click "PICK COLOR FROM CAR", then click the colour on the paint. A second click on another colour ADDS it.
Adjust the tolerance sliders until the edges are clean (about 30-50 is normal).

how_do_i.title: How do I sort or see my layers by colour?
steps: The LAYERS tab lists layers in the PSD's own order; there is no sort-by-colour. Use the "filter..." box at the top of the list to find a layer by name.
To work BY COLOUR instead: in Pro make a zone and use "PICK COLOR FROM CAR".

how_do_i.title: How do I find one layer in a long PSD?
steps: Open the LAYERS tab.
Type part of the name in the "filter..." box (top right of the list); Escape clears it.
Alt+click an eye icon to see only that layer.

how_do_i.title: How do I put a finish on the numbers?
steps: With a PSD: open the LAYERS tab and click the zone icon on the Numbers layer (it makes a zone limited to that layer). Then in BASE pick the finish.
Or make a zone and tick "Numbers" under RESTRICT TO LAYERS.
With a flat TGA: if the numbers are one clear colour, "+ Add Zone" > "PICK COLOR FROM CAR" and click a number.

how_do_i.title: How do I recolour the numbers?
steps: Quickest: in the AI panel type "numbers purple metallic".
In Pro make a zone for the numbers (see "put a finish on the numbers"), then in BASE set BASE COLOR to "Use solid color" and pick the colour.
To change the actual pixels instead use ADJUST > "Color Replace" on the Numbers layer.

how_do_i.title: How do I teach the app where the numbers are?
steps: Open the AI panel (the AI button bottom right) and ask for something on the numbers, e.g. "make the numbers gold".
It shows the car and asks. If its guess is right press "Yes, that is right".
If not press "No, I will show you", then draw a box around ONE number (a single one, not the whole panel). It finds the rest.
If the paint has none press "There are none on this paint".

how_do_i.title: How do I tell Shokker where the car's parts are (hood, roof, sides)?
steps: Ask the AI panel for a part change ("make the roof black"). If it does not know the car it shows the sheet and asks.
Draw a box around the part when asked (one part at a time) and say which part it is.
It remembers the car's parts from then on. The gear drawer can save or load a car map.

how_do_i.title: How do I make a colour or finish "pop" on the car?
steps: Select the zone, open BASE > Spec Sliders.
Click "Auto-Pop" (it nudges the spec toward glossy and metallic). Click again for more.
Or choose a "Spec preset..." such as Track Flash or Wet Candy.
Neighbouring areas in complementary colours help a finish read from far away.

how_do_i.title: How do I make the shine shinier without changing the colour (spec only)?
steps: Select the zone that covers the area (or make one).
In BASE choose a Foundation finish such as Chrome / Satin Chrome / Metallic / Pearl / Satin, and set the BASE COLOR dropdown to "Use source paint (spec only)".
Or keep your finish and open Spec Sliders: lower "G Rough" and raise "R Metal" for shinier, or click "Auto-Pop".
The colour preview may barely move; look at the spec channel views (R METAL, G ROUGH, B COAT) under the preview.

how_do_i.title: How do I make something matte (flat, no shine)?
steps: Select the zone, BASE > Base Material > Matte (or Flat Black for the deadest look).
Keep your colour: BASE COLOR "Use source paint (spec only)".
Or push "G Rough" up in Spec Sliders. Satin is the in-between.

how_do_i.title: How do I make something chrome?
steps: Select the zone, BASE > Base Material > Chrome (mirror) or Satin Chrome (softer).
Chrome repaints the zone silver. To keep your colours and only get the shine, use a Foundation chrome with "Use source paint (spec only)".
In iRacing the paint under a metal part should be near white for chrome to read.

how_do_i.title: How do I change a finish's colour?
steps: In BASE look at the BASE COLOR dropdown.
Plain finishes (gloss, matte, satin, candy, pearl, metallic) take a colour: choose "Use solid color" and pick it.
Finishes that bring their own colours (carbon, camo, holographic, flames ...) keep their look: use "Hue Shift" (and Saturation / Brightness) instead.

how_do_i.title: Why is the colour not applying to my finish?
steps: Check BASE COLOR. "Use finish's own color" ignores your colour; "Use source paint (spec only)" keeps the car's colour. Pick "Use solid color" to force one.
Some finishes bring their own palette (camo, carbon, holographic). A solid colour on those makes one flat colour and loses the pattern: use Hue Shift to recolour them.
A pattern in "Overlay" paint mode paints its own colours over yours: set Paint mode to "Blend" or use the pattern Hue slider.
If colours keep changing when you change finish, switch ON the Lock beside Base Color (or Color Lock in the picker).

how_do_i.title: How do I make a gradient (fade) between two colours?
steps: Select the zone and in BASE set BASE COLOR to "Custom gradient".
Set 2 colour stops (more for a sunset) and the direction.
The fade runs across the flat sheet, so each side of the car may fade differently; use one zone per side to control it.

how_do_i.title: How do I crush a pattern finer (smaller texture)?
steps: Select the zone, open PATTERN.
Drag "Scale" to the left (below 1.00x). Smaller means more repeats.
For the base finish's own texture use "Base Scale" in BASE.
On a whole car even normal-size patterns look big; 0.3x to 0.6x is typical for fine detail.

how_do_i.title: What does the Base Scale slider do?
steps: It changes how big the finish's own texture (flake, weave, grain) is inside that zone, from 0.05x to 5.0x (1.00x is normal).
Smaller = finer and more repeats; bigger = zoomed in.
It does not change colours or resize the car. Spec Scale follows it until you tick Independent Spec.

how_do_i.title: How do I add a pattern (carbon, flames, camo ...)?
steps: Select the zone, open PATTERN.
Click the pattern name box (shows "None") and choose a pattern.
Set "Paint mode": "Overlay" = the pattern's own colours cover the paint; "Blend" = it keeps your colour.
Use Opacity, Scale and Rotate to taste.

how_do_i.title: How do I remove a pattern?
steps: Select the zone, open PATTERN.
Click the small x ("Remove this pattern") beside the pattern name.

how_do_i.title: How do I rotate a pattern?
steps: PATTERN > "Rotate" slider (0-359 degrees) or type the number in the box beside it.
For the base finish texture use "Base Rotation" in BASE.

how_do_i.title: How do I move a pattern to a specific spot?
steps: In PATTERN find "Pattern placement" and click "Edit on Template" to drag it by hand, or "Fit to Zone".
For fine control open "Advanced Pattern Control Panel" and use Position X / Position Y, Flip H / Flip V.

how_do_i.title: How do I add a shiny texture without changing the colour (spec overlay)?
steps: Select the zone, open BASE > SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click "+ ADD SPEC OVERLAY" and choose a texture (brushed, hammered, scratched ...).
It changes shine and metal only. Check the R METAL / G ROUGH / B COAT views to see it.

how_do_i.title: How do I stack two finishes (second base)?
steps: Select the zone, open OVERLAYS.
Click the "2nd Base" box and pick a finish; use "+ Add 3rd overlay" for more (up to five layers).
Each overlay has its own blend controls.

how_do_i.title: How do I make a finish less strong (blend it with my paint)?
steps: BASE > "Base Strength": lower it. 0% = your original paint, 100% = full finish.
"Spec Strength" does the same for the shine only.

how_do_i.title: How do I change the order or priority of zones?
steps: In the left ZONES column drag a zone card by its handle (the three-line icon).
Top = highest priority; where two zones select the same pixels the higher one wins.
A catch-all "Remaining" zone belongs at the bottom.

how_do_i.title: Why is my zone not showing / doing anything?
steps: Does it have an area (colour, layer, or box) AND a finish? The panel warns "No color or region set yet".
Is a zone ABOVE it claiming the same pixels? Drag it higher.
Is the colour tolerance too tight? Raise it.
Is the zone muted (eye icon off) or limited to a hidden layer?
Is the preview stale? Press the Refresh button or F5.

how_do_i.title: Why is my preview not changing?
steps: Press F5 (or the "Refresh" button beside the preview) to force it.
Make sure the zone has an area and a finish, and nothing above it claims the same pixels.
Spec-only changes (shine, metal, coat) hardly change the colour preview: look at R METAL / G ROUGH / B COAT.
Make sure the view is not on SOURCE only: use SPLIT or CAR (buttons next to the zoom).
If it says "Preview failed - showing the LAST GOOD render", click that bar; reopen the app if it persists.

how_do_i.title: I loaded my paint and nothing happened. What now?
steps: Loading only shows your paint. Nothing changes until you give a zone a finish.
Click "+ Add Zone", pick a colour with "PICK COLOR FROM CAR", then choose a finish in BASE.
Or switch to CHAT and just say what you want.
Press RENDER at the end to write the files.

how_do_i.title: What do I do first? (a complete beginner)
steps: Load your paint: top row, SOURCE PAINT, "TGA/PNG/JPEG" (flat) or "PSD/XCF/ORA" (layers).
Make zones in PRO, or switch to CHAT to type what you want.
Pick looks, check the LIVE PREVIEW.
Set your iRacing customer ID and car folder at the top, then press RENDER.

how_do_i.title: How do I turn on the step-by-step tutorial (Training Wheels)?
steps: Click "Tutorial" in the top bar, or tick Training Wheels in Settings (the gear).
Follow the quests: load, zone, finish, render, then patterns, spec, overlays.
Click it again to turn it off.

how_do_i.title: What are layers?
steps: A layered PSD keeps parts of the livery on separate sheets: Car Paint (body colours), Numbers, Sponsors, Tape, Decals.
Layers let you change one thing (just the numbers) without touching the rest.
Template layers (Mask, Wire, Car_Mandatory) only show the car outlines and must be OFF when you render.
A flat TGA has no layers. Load a PSD ("PSD/XCF/ORA") to get them; see the LAYERS tab on the right.

how_do_i.title: How do I turn a layer on or off?
steps: Open the LAYERS tab.
Click the eye icon on the layer. Alt+click shows only that layer.

how_do_i.title: How do I switch off the template lines (Mask, Wire, Car_Mandatory) before exporting?
steps: LAYERS tab: click the eye on Car_Mandatory, Mask and Wire (the group "Turn Off Before Exporting TGA").
Then render. If lines still show on the car, one of them was left on.

how_do_i.title: How do I add a logo or sponsor picture?
steps: Open the LAYERS tab and click "+ Layer".
Choose a PNG / JPG / WebP / GIF (transparent PNG is best).
Drag it with Move (V) in LAYER mode, or use Transform (Ctrl+T) to size it.

how_do_i.title: How do I move or resize a number or logo?
steps: Click LAYER in the ZONE | LAYER switch (top toolbar).
Pick Move (V), click the number / logo (it isolates it), drag.
Use Transform (Ctrl+T) for size and rotation; "Apply" confirms.

how_do_i.title: How do I change a layer's opacity or blend mode?
steps: LAYERS tab, find the layer row.
Drag its opacity slider (or type a value), and use the blend dropdown (Normal, Multiply, Screen, Overlay ...).

how_do_i.title: How do I delete or duplicate a layer?
steps: LAYERS tab, use the layer's duplicate (Shift = offset copy) or delete icon.
Deleting removes the art; use the eye icon if you only want it hidden. Ctrl+Z undoes.

how_do_i.title: How do I merge or flatten layers?
steps: LAYERS tab > "Actions".
"Merge visible" combines the visible layers (hidden ones survive); "Flatten document" makes one layer and loses separation.

how_do_i.title: How do I paint on a layer by hand?
steps: Click LAYER in the ZONE | LAYER switch.
Pick Brush (B) and set size / opacity in the options bar (or open RETOUCH for Color Brush, Recolor, Smudge).
For a fresh blank layer: LAYERS tab > Actions > "+ Blank layer".

how_do_i.title: How do I make a zone follow one layer (restrict to a layer)?
steps: Select the zone, COLOR section > RESTRICT TO LAYERS, tick the layer(s).
Or press the zone icon on a layer row to make a new zone limited to it, or Ctrl+L to lock the active zone to the selected layer.

how_do_i.title: How do I keep sponsors and numbers untouched when I change the body?
steps: Make a zone for the body and tick only "Car Paint" under RESTRICT TO LAYERS.
Or in Chat say "change the body but leave the numbers alone".

how_do_i.title: How do I undo?
steps: Press Ctrl+Z, or the Undo button in the top toolbar (HISTORY menu).
To go back several steps open "Undo History...".
Under an AI panel answer press Undo to take back that whole answer.

how_do_i.title: How do I start over completely?
steps: Pro: left ZONES column > "Reset All Zones" (undoable, resets to the default zones).
One zone only: "Reset Zone" at the top of its panel.

how_do_i.title: How do I export my paint to iRacing?
steps: Top row: enter your iRacing customer number (IRACING USER ID) and set IRACING CAR FOLDER (use the car list button or browse).
Turn the template layers (Mask, Wire, Car_Mandatory) OFF.
Click RENDER (Ctrl+R). The paint and spec files are written to the car folder.
In iRacing press Alt+Tab, then Ctrl+R to reload paints.

how_do_i.title: How do I get Shokker to write straight into my iRacing folder every time?
steps: Set IRACING CAR FOLDER at the top: that alone copies every render there.
Settings (gear) > "Auto-deploy" only matters when the car folder is empty.

how_do_i.title: How do I choose my iRacing car?
steps: Top row, click the car-list button beside IRACING CAR FOLDER ("Pick detected iRacing car").
Choose your car (most recently painted first), or use the browse button.

how_do_i.title: What is my iRacing customer ID and where do I put it?
steps: It is your iRacing member number (4-7 digits), shown in your iRacing account.
Type it in IRACING USER ID at the top. It is part of the saved file names; a wrong one means iRacing shows nothing.

how_do_i.title: What is the difference between Custom Number and Sim-Stamped Number?
steps: Custom Number: the number is part of your paint (files car_num_ID.tga); iRacing adds none. Needs Hide Car Numbers ON in iRacing.
Sim-Stamped Number: iRacing stamps the number in the series font (files car_ID.tga). Do not also paint a number.
Switch at the top (CUSTOM NUMBER / SIM-STAMPED NUMBER).

how_do_i.title: Why doesn't my paint show in iRacing?
steps: Check the customer ID is right.
Check CUSTOM / SIM-STAMPED matches iRacing's Hide Car Numbers setting.
Check IRACING CAR FOLDER is the exact car folder.
Render again, then Alt+Tab and press Ctrl+R in iRacing.
Make sure the template layers were off and the file is a 2048 TGA.

how_do_i.title: How do I get my paint to look the same in iRacing as in Shokker?
steps: Remember the preview is a quick flat view; iRacing adds sun, shadow and its own stamps.
Chrome needs light paint under it and strong metal in the spec map.
Reload with Ctrl+R in iRacing; if the shine looks old move the old car_spec .mip file away.

how_do_i.title: What is a spec map?
steps: It is a second picture iRacing reads to know how shiny each pixel is.
Red = metal (255 = metal), Green = roughness (0 = mirror, 255 = matte), Blue = clearcoat (16 = best gloss, 255 = dull).
You see it under the preview as COMBINED, R METAL, G ROUGH, B COAT. RENDER writes both the paint and the spec file.

how_do_i.title: Where are the spec sliders?
steps: Click a zone card in the left column to open the ZONE POPOUT PANEL.
Open the BASE section and scroll to "Spec Sliders": R Metal, G Rough, B Coat.
Strength of the whole spec is "Spec Strength" higher up in BASE.

how_do_i.title: How do I see the spec map?
steps: Under the LIVE PREVIEW click COMBINED, R METAL, G ROUGH or B COAT.
Click one to open it larger, or use "Channels" for exact numbers.

how_do_i.title: How do I read the exact metal / rough / coat of a spot?
steps: Top toolbar > SPEC TOOLS > "Material Sampler...".
Click a spot on the spec map: M / R / CC values appear; "Apply to Active Zone" copies them to the zone.

how_do_i.title: How do I make numbers and sponsors read cleanly under chrome or candy?
steps: Top toolbar > SPEC TOOLS > "Decal Rescue Kit...".
Choose Flat Vinyl, Satin Decal or Gloss Decal. It puts a plain non-metal spec under stamped numbers and sponsors.

how_do_i.title: How do I make fake grille holes or vents (lighting mask)?
steps: Top toolbar > SPEC TOOLS > "Lighting Mask...".
Choose Use Source Alpha, Full Lighting, Reduced Lighting or Kill Lighting for the area.

how_do_i.title: How do I pick or change a finish for a zone?
steps: Select the zone, BASE > click the Base Material box.
Search by name or idea (try "gold chrome" or #carbon), or tap a #tag chip.
Preview on the On-Car Stage, then press "USE IT". "Surprise me" rolls a random good one.

how_do_i.title: How do I search the whole finish library?
steps: Click the FINISHES tab on the right (full-screen library).
Type in the search box: names, ideas ("icy blue"), or #tags; use the filters and the star for favourites.

how_do_i.title: How do I get ideas for a finish I can't name?
steps: In the AI panel describe the feel ("like a rainy city night, but glossier") and it offers several real finishes with previews.
Or open the Base Material picker and press "Surprise me".

how_do_i.title: How do I apply a ready-made look (preset)?
steps: Left column > "More" (three dots) > "Presets Gallery".
Click a preset to apply it.

how_do_i.title: How do I give every zone the same finish?
steps: Pick the finish on one zone.
Left column > More > "Apply Finish to All".

how_do_i.title: How do I duplicate a zone?
steps: On the zone card in the left column click the copy icon.
Change the area or finish of the copy.

how_do_i.title: How do I hide a zone for a moment?
steps: Click the eye icon on its card in the ZONES column. Click again to bring it back.

how_do_i.title: How do I delete a zone?
steps: Click the x on the zone's card (Ctrl+Z undoes). The Chat copilot cannot delete zones.

how_do_i.title: How do I draw the exact area a zone covers (a box or lasso)?
steps: In the zone's APPLY AREA click "Draw box" or "Lasso".
Drag on the paint. "Clear" removes it, "Activate" turns it back on.

how_do_i.title: How do I use the magic wand or lasso to select an area?
steps: Pick Wand (W) in the top toolbar (or Lasso L / Rect O). Click or drag on the paint.
Shift adds, Alt subtracts; the Tolerance slider sets how similar colours must be.
Select a zone in the left column and press "Use Region" to give it that selection.

how_do_i.title: How do I select a number or logo as a whole?
steps: Top toolbar > SELECT menu > "Grab Object" (G).
Click inside a solid part of the number; its outline is selected.
Use "Use Region" on the zone you want.

how_do_i.title: How do I grow, shrink or soften a selection edge?
steps: Top toolbar > MASK menu: "Grow 1 px / 2 px", "Shrink", "Fill Holes", "Feather 2 px", "Smooth Edges", "Invert Mask".
The same buttons sit in the bar under the canvas (Grow, Shrink, Feather, Smooth).

how_do_i.title: How do I invert or copy a zone's area?
steps: Top toolbar > MASK: "Invert Mask" swaps selected / unselected, "Copy Mask" copies it to another zone, "Mirror Mask" flips it left-right.

how_do_i.title: How do I remove one spot from a zone's colour match?
steps: Top toolbar > MASK > "Exclude Region", then paint over the bits to leave out (red overlay).
"Include Region" paints bits to keep (green); "Erase Spatial" removes those strokes.

how_do_i.title: How do I zoom and move around the canvas?
steps: Buttons beside the canvas: zoom out, +, FIT (Ctrl+0), 1:1 (actual size).
Ctrl+plus / Ctrl+minus also zoom.

how_do_i.title: How do I compare before and after?
steps: Click "B/A" (or press B) to flip between the last preview and now.
"Compare" gives a wipe slider; SPLIT shows source and preview side by side.

how_do_i.title: How do I see the car preview bigger?
steps: Click the preview picture to open it full size (PAINT / SPEC MAP).

how_do_i.title: How do I save my project and come back later?
steps: Click "Save / Open" in the top toolbar (SPB Projects). It saves the paint (PSD included), every zone and layer settings in one file.
To reopen, click "Save / Open" again and load it.

how_do_i.title: How do I share my finish setup with someone?
steps: After RENDER the recipe card appears: "Copy Card" (paste into Discord), "Save Card PNG", "Share Recipe" (a .shokkerrecipe file) or "Copy TP Desc" (Trading Paints description).
Others load it with "Import Recipe" in the top toolbar.

how_do_i.title: How do I load a recipe someone sent me?
steps: Top toolbar > "Import Recipe".
Choose the .shokkerrecipe file; its zones, colours and finishes are applied to your car.

how_do_i.title: How do I save a zone layout as a template?
steps: Left column > More > "Save as Template", name it, Save.
Load it later from the "Load Template..." dropdown in the same menu.

how_do_i.title: How do I go back to an earlier render?
steps: Top toolbar > RENDER HISTORY > "Recent" or "Gallery", click a thumbnail to restore it with its full recipe.
To keep one safe, press "Save to keep" on the recipe card.

how_do_i.title: How do I save a zip of my paint files?
steps: Settings (gear) > tick the ZIP option. Every render bundles the paint TGA, spec TGA and preview.

how_do_i.title: How do I export the spec channels as pictures (for Photoshop)?
steps: Left column > More > "PNG Channels Export" (choose the export folder first).
Or LAYERS tab > Actions > "Photoshop round-trip" to export layers and bring a TGA back.

how_do_i.title: How do I use the Chat mode / AI panel?
steps: Click CHAT in the pill (or the AI button bottom right).
Type what you want: "make the hood matte black", "retro red white and blue stripes", "numbers gold chrome". Enter sends.
Each answer has an Undo button; "Another take" tries a different idea.

how_do_i.title: How do I talk to Claude about my paint through MCP?
steps: Open the AI panel, press the gear, switch ON "Let an AI assistant (Claude or ChatGPT/Codex) control Shokker Paint Booth".
Press "Install in Claude Desktop" and restart Claude Desktop.
With Shokker open, ask Claude: "Using Shokker Paint Booth, give me a Gulf-style livery".
Every change shows in the AI panel with an Undo button. No API key needed; your Claude plan is used.

how_do_i.title: How do I use ChatGPT / Codex with Shokker?
steps: AI panel > gear > bridge settings > "Connect ChatGPT / Codex", review, then "Add SPB to Codex settings".
Restart Codex, sign in with ChatGPT, choose a model, chat with Shokker open.
Use "Take over in SPB" before asking the in-app copilot while an outside assistant has control.

how_do_i.title: How do I give the in-app copilot an AI key (and which model)?
steps: AI panel > gear.
Paste your OpenRouter key and pick the one model offered (DeepSeek v4.1 Flash is recommended). A daily cap protects your spend.
Without a key the built-in designer still handles common requests.

how_do_i.title: What can the AI copilot NOT do?
steps: It cannot delete zones, open or save files, import a paint, export to iRacing, or hand-paint.
It can tell you the exact buttons to click. Every change it makes has an Undo.

how_do_i.title: How do I make a livery from a description (retro stripes, Gulf style ...)?
steps: Open the AI panel and describe it: "retro red white and blue stripes, flat with chrome trim" or "black and gold two-tone".
Refine: "thinner", "make the red orange", "matte", "another take".
Press Undo under any answer to go back.

how_do_i.title: How do I copy the look of a picture?
steps: In the AI panel click the paper-clip (Attach a picture) and choose the livery, logo or flag.
Ask it to copy the design or the colours. Needs an AI key; check the preview and refine.

how_do_i.title: How do I change the on-screen size of the buttons?
steps: Top row, the minus and plus buttons beside the percentage ("UI Smaller / UI Larger"). They resize the toolbars, not the canvas.

how_do_i.title: How do I see the keyboard shortcuts?
steps: Press ? or Settings (gear) > "Keyboard Shortcuts".

how_do_i.title: How do I move the finish library or panels out of the way?
steps: Click the small arrow at the edge of the left or right column to collapse it. Press E to show / hide the zone editor.

how_do_i.title: How do I fix a stuck or blank preview?
steps: Press F5 or the "Refresh" button.
Click the red "Preview failed" bar if shown.
Close and reopen the app if the engine says it is offline.

how_do_i.title: Why won't the RENDER button start?
steps: Is a paint loaded? Does the Source Paint box have a full path?
Did you enter your iRacing customer ID (4-7 digits)?
Does every zone you want have BOTH a colour/area and a finish? A message says which does not.
Is another render still running? Wait a minute.

how_do_i.title: How do I recolour artwork on the paint itself (not just a finish)?
steps: Top toolbar > ADJUST > "Hue / Saturation" (shift every colour) or "Color Replace" (one colour to another).
In LAYER mode these edit the selected layer.

how_do_i.title: How do I add text (lettering) to the paint?
steps: There is no Text button in the main tool row. The easiest way: make the lettering as a transparent PNG (or in your PSD in Photoshop) and add it with LAYERS tab > "+ Layer".
Then move and size it with Move (V) and Transform (Ctrl+T) in LAYER mode.
For a PSD, edit the text layer in Photoshop and re-open it with "Open Layered".

how_do_i.title: How do I use the eyedropper to match a colour on the car?
steps: Pick Color (P) in the toolbar, choose the zone in the box that appears, click the colour on the SOURCE picture.
"+ Add Color" adds it to the zone; "Set" replaces the zone's colour.

how_do_i.title: How do I make a car side different from the other side?
steps: Make one zone per side with APPLY AREA > "Draw box" around each side's panel on the flat sheet.
Give each its own finish or colour; both sides are separate rectangles.
Or in Chat say "make the left side matte black" if the car's parts are known.

how_do_i.title: What are Foundation finishes and what is a "brings its own colours" finish?
steps: Foundation (f_) finishes change only the shine; with "Use source paint (spec only)" they leave your colours alone.
Plain bases (gloss, matte, satin, candy, pearl, metallic) take the zone colour.
Special finishes (carbon, camo, holographic, flames ...) bring their own colours: recolour them with Hue Shift, not a solid colour.

how_do_i.title: How do I know what the base finishes do?
steps: Gloss = standard shiny paint, Matte = flat, Satin = soft sheen, Chrome = mirror, Candy = deep tinted gloss, Pearl = shimmer, Metallic = flake.
Hover or tap a finish in the picker to read what it does.

how_do_i.title: How do I make a finish more or less glossy?
steps: Spec Sliders: "G Rough" lower = glossier, higher = duller.
"B Coat" sets the clearcoat glass look. "Spec Strength" scales it all.

how_do_i.title: How do I fix numbers or sponsors that look wrong under a special finish?
steps: Make sure the body zone is limited to "Car Paint" under RESTRICT TO LAYERS so numbers are not covered.
Use SPEC TOOLS > "Decal Rescue Kit..." if they read sparkly or dull.

how_do_i.title: How do I get started with a PSD that has many layers and I'm overwhelmed?
steps: Turn on Training Wheels ("Tutorial").
In Pro use the "filter..." box in the LAYERS tab and ignore Mask / Wire / Car_Mandatory.

how_do_i.title: How do I use SPEC SCULPT?
steps: Click "SPEC SCULPT" in the top row for the guided look library of spec-only effects.
After saving a Sculpt spec the main RENDER keeps that spec; clear the imported spec map in Settings to go back to zone shine.

how_do_i.title: How do I import art or a pack (Shokk Drop)?
steps: Click "Shokk Drop" in the top row.
Import art, Import DNA spec, or share .spbdrop packs.

how_do_i.title: How do I randomise a look for ideas?
steps: Left column > More > "Rand Current Zone" or "Rand All Zones".
In the picker, "Surprise me" rolls one good finish. Ctrl+Z undoes.

how_do_i.title: What is NOT in Shokker today (animation, other sims, 3D view, a shop, live Photoshop sync, Mac)?
steps: Honest answer: that is not available in Shokker today. Not in the app: animated or moving paints, glow-in-the-dark paint (iRacing has no emissive paint), other sims (Shokker writes iRacing paint + spec TGAs only), a 3D car view or painting on a 3D model, a shop or marketplace to sell paints, live sync with Photoshop while you edit, and a Mac version (Windows only).
Nearest thing you can do: render, then look at the car in iRacing's own 3D paint viewer; for Photoshop, save your PSD and load it again with "PSD/XCF/ORA" (top row, SOURCE PAINT).
Everything else - colours, finishes, patterns, spec - is in Pro; ask "how do I ..." for the steps.
